acceptance_criteria.requirement: Holding the interact input while stationary, in range, and undamaged for the full configured duration (default 5.0s) opens the door and permits crossing the doorway.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Play Mode test: drive the interaction start method on the interaction component, advance simulated time by 5+ seconds without cancelling, assert IsOpen becomes true and progress reaches 1.0.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Door opening progress is exposed as a public normalized float (0 to 1) that increases monotonically while an uninterrupted interaction is held.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Play Mode test: begin interaction, advance time to 2 of 5 seconds, assert progress is approximately 0.4 within tolerance of ±0.05.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Releasing the interact input before completion cancels the attempt and resets progress to exactly 0.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Play Mode test: begin interaction, advance partial time, call the public release/end method, assert progress equals 0 and IsOpen is false.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Player movement during an active, incomplete interaction cancels the attempt and resets progress to exactly 0.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Play Mode test: begin interaction, advance partial time, invoke the public movement-cancellation entry point directly (not via WASD polling), assert progress equals 0 and IsOpen is false.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Player damage during an active, incomplete interaction cancels the attempt and resets progress to exactly 0.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Play Mode test: begin interaction, advance partial time, call the health component's public TakeDamage method, assert progress equals 0 and IsOpen is false.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Interaction state (start, cancel, progress, completion) is driven entirely through public C# methods/properties that do not require simulated keyboard or Input System device events, so tests can drive it deterministically.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Code review of the Play Mode test file: confirm every test calls public methods/properties on the interaction/door components and none inject InputSystem device events or legacy Input calls.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: A visible UI prompt appears while the player is inside the door's interaction trigger zone and is hidden when the player leaves that zone.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Manual Unity Play Mode check: move the placeholder player into and out of the trigger zone and observe the prompt UI element's visibility toggle.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: A visible progress indicator (UI Slider or Image with fillAmount) reflects the normalized progress value in real time while the interaction is active.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Manual Unity Play Mode check: hold the interact key near the door and observe the indicator animate from empty to full over 5 seconds.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Interaction duration is a serialized, Inspector-configurable field defaulting to 5.0 seconds, with no duplicate hardcoded duration elsewhere in the completion check.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Code review: confirm a single [SerializeField] float duration field with default value 5f is the sole source used in the completion comparison.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: The Editor menu command 'No Safe Circle/Build Door Prototype Scene' generates a complete, playable scene at Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity containing a floor, player placeholder, sealed door/doorway, camera, lighting, interaction UI, and a documented damage-test control, with all serialized references auto-wired.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Manual execution: run the menu command from a clean state, inspect the Hierarchy and Inspector for the listed objects and populated references, then run it again and confirm no console errors and no duplicated hierarchy.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Running the scene-builder command a second time does not create duplicate GameObjects, UI elements, or scenes, and leaves no null-reference errors in the Console.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Manual execution: run the menu command twice consecutively from an already-built scene state; diff the Hierarchy object count before and after the second run and confirm it is unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Once the door-opening interaction completes, the doorway no longer blocks player movement through it.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Manual Play Mode check: complete the interaction, then walk the placeholder player through the doorway and confirm no collision blocking occurs.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: No excluded systems (enemy AI, NavMesh, ranged enemies, Frost Field, Force Wave, Fireball, door locking/durability/breaking, multiple rooms, custom art, external packages) are present anywhere in the delivered feature.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Search Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/ for such systems and diff Packages/manifest.json against its pre-implementation contents to confirm it is unchanged.

required_files.purpose: Core door component: serialized duration (default 5s), normalized progress (0-1), open/closed state, and StartInteraction/CancelInteraction/Tick-style completion logic exposed through a public API independent of raw input polling

Detects proximity to the door's trigger zone, reads interact input via the new Input System, and calls DoorInteractable's public start/cancel API; exposes a public method to signal movement-triggered cancellation
WASD movement for the placeholder player using the new Input System; notifies PlayerInteractionController when movement occurs so an active interaction can be cancelled
Minimal damage component exposing a public TakeDamage method, used by the debug damage control and by Play Mode tests to trigger interaction cancellation
Binds DoorInteractable's in-range and progress state to the UI prompt and progress-fill elements
Editor menu command 'No Safe Circle/Build Door Prototype Scene' that idempotently generates DoorPrototype.unity with all required objects, UI, and wired serialized references
Generated prototype scene, produced only by the scene-builder command and never hand-authored
Play Mode tests covering completion, movement cancellation, damage cancellation, and interaction-release cancellation
Assembly definition for the runtime gameplay scripts
Assembly definition for the Editor scene-builder script
Assembly definition for the Play Mode test assembly, referencing the runtime assembly and the Unity Test Framework
This planning contract; the sole approved source of implementation scope for the next agent
Implementer's record of files changed, design decisions, scene-generation instructions, test instructions, known limitations, and confirmation that excluded systems were not implemented

risks: activeInputHandler is set to 1 (Input System Package (New) only) in ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset; any use of legacy UnityEngine.Input by the implementer will throw InvalidOperationException at runtime — the implementer must use UnityEngine.InputSystem (e.g., Keyboard.current) exclusively

Scene-builder idempotency is nontrivial: a naive re-run could duplicate GameObjects, UI canvases, or EventSystems unless the builder explicitly finds-and-replaces known objects by name before creating new ones

Coupling movement detection to interaction cancellation risks scope creep into a general-purpose player controller; the implementation must stay a small, focused component limited to this prototype's needs
The debug damage-test control must be clearly labeled as a testing/demo affordance so it is not mistaken for a combat system, which would blur the boundary with out-of-scope enemy/combat content
The five-second timer must be measured via accumulated Time.deltaTime (not frame counts) so Play Mode tests that advance simulated time remain deterministic and frame-rate independent

Presence of the Unity Test Framework package is unconfirmed in the provided manifest excerpt; if it is missing, Play Mode tests cannot compile until it is enabled, and the implementer must flag this rather than silently omitting tests

Scene generation and final visual/interaction correctness are Editor-only concerns that cannot be verified by this planning agent; per CLAUDE.md, human inspection and Play Mode execution remain required before the feature is considered complete

test_cases.name: Completion opens the door
test_cases.setup: DoorInteractable and PlayerInteractionController exist with the default 5s duration; the player is in range, undamaged, and stationary.
test_cases.action: Call the controller's public BeginInteraction method, then advance simulated time by 5+ seconds without calling any cancel method.
test_cases.expected: DoorInteractable.Progress reaches 1.0 and DoorInteractable.IsOpen becomes true; the doorway no longer blocks a test object moved through it.

test_cases.name: Movement cancels the attempt
test_cases.setup: Same as above; begin interaction and advance simulated time to approximately 2 seconds (progress ~0.4).
test_cases.action: Call the movement-cancellation entry point (e.g., PlayerInteractionController.OnPlayerMoved) directly.
test_cases.expected: DoorInteractable.Progress resets to 0 and IsOpen remains false.

test_cases.name: Damage cancels the attempt
test_cases.setup: Same as above; begin interaction and advance simulated time to approximately 2 seconds.
test_cases.action: Call PlayerHealth.TakeDamage with any positive amount on the player's health component.
test_cases.expected: DoorInteractable.Progress resets to 0 and IsOpen remains false.

test_cases.name: Releasing interaction cancels the attempt
test_cases.setup: Same as above; begin interaction and advance simulated time to approximately 2 seconds.
test_cases.action: Call the controller's public EndInteraction (release) method.
test_cases.expected: DoorInteractable.Progress resets to 0 and IsOpen remains false.

test_cases.name: Progress reflects normalized elapsed time
test_cases.action: Advance simulated time to exactly 2.5 seconds without cancelling.
test_cases.expected: DoorInteractable.Progress is approximately 0.5, within a tolerance of ±0.05.
